findings.title: Cleanup now runs ten times as often
findings.body: This changes the global cleanup scheduler from every 10 minutes to every minute, although the PR only addresses annotation cleanup. Every cleanup job—not just annotation cleanup—will therefore run much more frequently, increasing database and filesystem load; if a run takes longer than a minute, a queued tick can also trigger another run immediately afterward.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: This logs at error level unconditionally, including when `err` is nil and when the query finds no IDs. Normal cleanup cycles will therefore produce error-level log entries (and include potentially large ID lists), creating misleading alerts and unnecessary log volume. The other new cleanup batch logs at lines 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579 have the same issue.

findings.title: Building the inline ID list has quadratic cost
findings.body: Each iteration formats a new string containing the entire accumulated ID list. For a configured batch of N IDs, this repeatedly copies the growing string, giving quadratic allocation and CPU cost. Large batches take this SQLite path (the new test configures 32,767), so cleanup can incur substantial avoidable work; build the list with a builder or join instead.
